### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**60** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aa347d082214b0ff47d6ca657299c728f29d29b9` — the merge of head `2b295cabd4d838576682f001485858831f0be334` into base `8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aa347d082214b0ff47d6ca657299c728f29d29b9 && git checkout aa347d082214b0ff47d6ca657299c728f29d29b9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1 2b295cabd4d838576682f001485858831f0be334 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1 && git merge --no-ff 2b295cabd4d838576682f001485858831f0be334

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8fbbd5082f3fcde0d972c76cfcd4d286c4eb4fa1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `070d81252b3c534540607a78cd6e8782808efaa2`
Local-runs: none

Reviewer: an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`epic:#15194`), read-only: the diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-24590` (merge-base `04669a467`, `origin/main` at `5a871e4e4`), the PR body, card #24530 with claim 6267470053 and os-dev-report 6270530684, rulings 6266750393 / 6267391172 / 6270035914 on #15194, ruling 6257510973 (#24377, Q4 A), step 0's measured plan 6268559156 (#24522), the merged harness and its fixture on `origin/main`, AGENTS.md, `scripts/check-changeset-*.mjs`, and the head's check-runs. The head did not move while this was written. The `--paths` reading of the file list is the schema face (one published-schema hit, `platform-object-names.ts`); the brief asks for the narrowing face, and both map to this tier. The prose faces (`.changeset/`, `content/docs/`) are read against the diff below and are no remainder.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Fresh install — PASS.** `sys-platform-setting-audit.object.ts:44-47` declares `managedBy: 'engine-owned'`, `systemFields: { tenant: false }` and `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`, with `enable.apiMethods: ['get', 'list']` (:167-171): the same posture as `sys_platform_setting.object.ts:53-57, :148`. The D7 family pin (`deployment-level-no-tenant-column.test.ts:39-40`, the new row) asserts no injected or declared `organization_id`, the `systemFields` opt-out and the platform-scoped capability, so the created table has no organization column; the regenerated census (`scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`, `sys_platform_setting_audit`, `reach: out`, reason `systemFields.tenant: false`) says the same from the registered schema. The read door is right: `SETTINGS_READ_DOOR_OBJECTS` (`settings-read-door.ts:44-49`) gains the sibling and `registerSettingsReadDoor` (:99-106) iterates that list, so the namespace predicate is ANDed into every `find`/`findOne`/`count`/`aggregate` on it; the read-door pin seeds a sibling row per namespace (`settings-read-door.pin.test.ts:131-136`) and its per-object `for (const object of SETTINGS_READ_DOOR_OBJECTS)` battery and the by-name registration check (`hasObjectMiddleware`) now cover it. Who may read a new global-rung row: a system context, or a principal holding `manage_platform_settings` (object permission) whose capabilities also satisfy the namespace's `readPermission`. Every stock global manifest (`ai`, `auth`, `knowledge`, `mail`, `sms`, `storage` in `service-settings/src/manifests/`, and objectql's `lifecycle-settings.ts:23-24`) already names `manage_platform_settings` as its `readPermission`, so the door, the setting and its trail agree.

**(b) 18.0 database — PASS, the report's claim verified.** The writer routes by rung only (`settings-service-plugin.ts:553-573`, `settingAuditObjectFor`), and `sys-setting-audit.object.ts` is untouched: its `scope` select keeps `global`, so the 18.0 global rows stay readable where they are. I looked for every reader of settings history: in this repo the non-test mentions of `sys_setting_audit` are the writer, the read door, `settings-service.ts` docblocks (:1333, :1859) and `config-change-audit.ts` prose; there is no route, service method or in-process reader that lists audit rows. In `../objectui` (at `78b07f4`) no source names `sys_setting_audit`, a settings history view or an audit grid, and the console bundle under `packages/console/dist` carries no such string. The only readers are the generic data-API grids `GET /data/sys_setting_audit` and `GET /data/sys_platform_setting_audit`, both behind the read door, and the dogfood pin reads the 18.0 row through the first and the new row through the second (`settings-audit-global-rung-sibling.dogfood.test.ts:139-155`). Nothing that showed a global-rung row before stops showing it. A reader that wants the global rung's whole history reads both tables, selected by `scope = 'global'`: F3 holds (the fixture's 4 `sys_setting_audit` rows all carry `org_mvf8cxynmka5sb9b`), and the pins select by scope, never by a NULL organization (`settings-deployment-level-expand.test.ts:205-224`). Not building a union API is also what ADR-0131 D7's Presentation rule asks: no surface merges two sources server-side.

**(c) Nothing moves, deletes or re-stamps 18.0 rows; no column drops — PASS.** The diff touches no ceremony, apply, migration or schema-sync code; `organization-ownership-apply.ts` and its `MOVES` table are unchanged; the only inventory change is one added row for the new table (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:622-628`). The dogfood pin's case B boots HEAD over a database holding an 18.0-shaped stamped global row and asserts, after the stack stops, that the row is still in `sys_setting_audit` with its organization (`:157-164`). The harness's own case 3 would red on any 18.0 row moved or re-stamped (`upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts:101-120`).

**(d) R1–R4 and the boot guard (F2) — PASS.** F2: `sys-secret.object.ts` is blob `6c09998…` on both `origin/main` and the head, and `service-automation/src/sys-flow-credential.object.ts` is blob `daa0672…` on both: byte-identical, neither flipped; no file in the diff changes either object's tenancy, and their inventory rows keep `fate: 'attribution'`. The guard: `findV17ShapeTables` (`organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts:196-218`) flags an object with `systemFields.tenant === false`, no declared `organization_id`, and a PHYSICAL `organization_id` column; the sibling is created fresh by `createTable` from a declaration with no such column, and on an 18.0 database the table does not exist before sync (`pragma_table_info` of a missing table answers no rows), so it can never be flagged. The guard's code is untouched, so R3 (v17 refused with the guard's code) and R4 (walled posture refused) are the same code paths as on `main`; the dogfood pin composes `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin` and the audit plugin on both boots. R1 is the dogfood pin's case A plus the report's fresh showcase boot. R2: the fixture's reshaped `sys_setting_audit` rows (`id`, `organization_id` ×4) are never written by this PR; the dev ran the harness 5/5 at `f6128e3`, which IS the head #24552 merged as `ec16dbe2e`. What remains procedural, not a code defect, is in ③: the PR head has not merged `main` since `ec16dbe2e`, so the merged harness has not run on this tree in CI (and cannot: dogfood is `main`-only in CI and #24554's opt-in lane is unmerged).

**(e) Complete feature (6270035914) — PASS.** New installs write the new shape through a live predicate; the sibling is registered in the service manifest (`manifest.ts:29`), the read door and `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE`; the 18.0 shape is still read. Nothing is dormant or waits for a later PR to switch it on; what is deferred (the move of the 18.0 global rows) is deferred by the line's own expand-first rule and is written down table by table. Each insert names its table literally (`settings-service-plugin.ts:647-658`), so the tenant-audit census stays statically decidable (one new `elevated` site, counts regenerated: 231 → 232).

**(f) The open questions — all five "A" readings are sound.** (1) Reverting the `sys_secret` / `sys_flow_credential` flip: correct under F2 and flags[0]; measured both spellings and the ceremony-class block. (2) No union reader: correct, there was none to union, and D7 forbids a merged list. (3) Name and shape: `sys_platform_setting_audit` mirrors `sys_platform_setting`; the field set, indexes and `enable` block match `sys_setting_audit`'s one for one, with `scope` kept as a one-option select so one reader reads both tables with the same columns, which is what step 0's plan asked ("same fields"). (4) One PR, `Closes #24530`: consistent with 6270035914 item 2, which already places the deferred flips in the steps 5+6 landing. (5) Changeset disposition: judged in ②.

Minor, non-blocking: `settings-service.ts:1333` still names three read-door objects in prose, and `config-change-audit.test.ts:465`'s describe title still says "`sys_setting_audit` keeps its rows" while the helper now reads the sibling — cosmetic. The sibling, like `sys_platform_setting`, `sys_metadata_commit` and `sys_migration_journal`, is outside the platform-objects i18n extract roster (`i18n-extract.config.ts:190`, `bundle-ownership.test.ts:19-42`), so its labels ship untranslated; that mirrors the precedent and no gate asks otherwise.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/24530-settings-audit-global-rung-sibling.md`; four touched published packages (`platform-objects`, `service-settings`, `spec`, `cli`) at `minor`; `@objectstack/dogfood` is private. The `yes` arm is earned (a new object, a new exported predicate and two constants, a new registry name) and `minor` satisfies the LEVEL axis. The `narrowing` arm is BREAKING and is carried as the launch-window convention requires: `!` in the title, the **BREAKING** banner, before/now/remedy in the body, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a documented category (ADR-0087 :735); the body carries no FROM → TO block, so the category's refusal does not fire, and `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. The narrowing is real but small: a principal who could list a global-rung audit row in `sys_setting_audit` by object grant alone (a host whose engine offers no middleware seam, or a host-registered global manifest with a weaker `readPermission`) now needs `manage_platform_settings`; for every stock global namespace the read door already demanded it. Declaring it as a narrowing is the safe side. ADR-0087 has nothing to rewrite: no metadata key is removed or renamed, and `sys_setting_audit.scope` keeps its `global` option because 18.0 rows hold it. Level and arm agree with the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **ceremony_owes (step 5+6 landing, #24581/#24582):** `sys_setting_audit` rows `WHERE scope = 'global'` move to `sys_platform_setting_audit` — a `departures` entry on its inventory row and a `MOVES` entry in `organization-ownership-apply.ts` in the shape of `sys_setting`'s `global-rung-move` (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:606-619`, `-apply.ts:597-603`), selected by scope, never by NULL (F3); then `scope`'s `global` option may retire and 8e's NOT NULL applies to the rest. `sys_secret` and `sys_flow_credential`: the `systemFields: { tenant: false }` flip, inventory fate 3 → `column-drop`, and the `column-drops` step, in the same release as the open ceremony (F2); the settings writer stops passing `organization_id` for `sys_secret`. Step 7 (#24583): remove the dual read. The seat carries these onto the cards' bodies; nothing in this PR records them in code, by design.
- **Merge gate still owed (6267391172 item 3):** the head's merge-base is `04669a467`; `main` gained `ec16dbe2e` (the harness) afterwards and the head has not merged it (`refs/review/pr-24590` holds no `upgrade-18x-harness` files). The merge preview is clean (`mergeable: true`; no `main` commit since the merge-base touches the regenerable artefacts), but R2 on the merged tree rests on a re-run after `main` is merged: dogfood shards are skipped on PRs, and #24554's `needs:upgrade-harness` lane is an unmerged Tier H draft. The PR is correctly still a draft.
- **Card #24530 closes with one of its three named parts delivered.** The other two are placed in the steps 5+6 landing by 6270035914; the seat confirms #24582's body names both flips and the `sys_setting_audit` move before this PR lands and closes the card.
- **ADR-0131 D7's dated note for Q4 A** (`docs/adr/0131-…md:553-556` on `origin/main`) says the `sys_setting_audit` half "has not shipped"; it ships with this landing. `docs/adr/**` is Tier H and outside the claim's surface; the seat batches the one-line status change into the next Tier H ADR PR.
- **Checklist re-points** (`platform-core.json` items `settings-hub-roundtrip` rev 5 and `settings-audit-secret-fingerprint` rev 3) are outside the claim's named surface, follow from the change, and are right: `localization.timezone` is tenant-scope and stays in `sys_setting_audit`; `mail` is global and its rows now land in the sibling.
- **Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts), read at 15:37Z and once more at 15:39Z:** 40 runs, 29 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, the three dogfood shards, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke: the `main`-only and opt-in lanes), 0 failed, 6 still `in_progress` — Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, 6/6 and TypeScript Type Check. Green already: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, every Lint lane, Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check · workspace / source / consumer / debt ledger, Test Core 5/6, Spec property liveness, the three claim guards. This PASS is rendered on the code and the completed runs; it stands only if the six in-flight runs conclude `success` — a red among them re-opens the verdict for this head, and the seat re-reads before adopting.
